seats: a secular academic scholar of the Bible

fixes.row: Said as still to come, or to the end: "will be saved", "if you hold firmly", "to the end"
fixes.why: Three Hebrew promises to Judah and Israel ("Judah will be saved") sit in a row whose label and note belong to the NT question of perseverance ("to the end", "if you hold firmly") and whose sibling row is about "you have been saved". Hebrew has no tense in that sense; filing a promise to a nation under 'still to come' beside 'if you hold firmly' reads a later question back into it.
fixes.fix: Keep the three verses but add to the row's note: "Jer 23:6, 30:7 and 33:16 are promises to Judah and Israel; they are not part of the question of falling away." Alternatively move them to 'The LORD saves his people and gives them victory'. Also add to the note of both tense rows that the counts (10 and 23) follow the Greek forms, not the weight of either side.

fixes.row: Said as still to come, or to the end / Said as done, or going on
fixes.why: The row label mixes a grammatical category (future 'will be saved') with a condition ('if you hold firmly', 'to the end'). 1 Cor 15:2 is a present tense verb with a condition and is in both rows. 1 Cor 3:15 and 5:5 are about the same man/work and are not statements about final salvation in the way 'to the end' suggests. The label says more than the verse forms do.
fixes.fix: Relabel row 18 to what is on the surface: "Said with 'will be': 'will be saved', 'if you hold firmly', 'to the end'" and row 17 "Said with 'have been' or 'are being': ...". Keep 1 Cor 15:2 in both (the note already says why).

fixes.row: Saved from sins, wrath, death, uncleanness, "this corrupt generation"
fixes.why: The first examples shown are Matt 1:21 and Rom 5:9; the Hebrew Scriptures' own verses (Ezek 36:29 'save you from all your uncleanness', Ezek 37:23, Ps 68:20 'escape from death') come after and read as the lesser echo. Matt 1:21 is also repeated from the Jesus row, so the row's eight verses are four NT, four Hebrew and the order puts the NT first.
fixes.fix: Order the Hebrew verses first (Ezek 36:29, 37:23, Ps 68:20 then NT), so the examples a reader sees begin with Ezek 36:29 and Matt 1:21 only second. Same rule for the whole hub: wherever a row holds both testaments, the first four examples should lead with the Hebrew.

fixes.row: Saved from sins ... / Save a life, a soul
fixes.why: Both rows say 'saved from X' with different X: Jas 5:20 'save his soul from death' and Ps 109:31 'from the condemners of his soul' are in both. 'Life/soul' in Hebrew nefesh and Greek psyche is 'the person who is in danger', and the sense is not separate from 'from death'. Two rows of 8-9 for one idea.
fixes.fix: Merge into one row 'Saved from sins, wrath, death, uncleanness; a life, a soul' (about 15 verses). The label for the merged row keeps both lists in the text's words.

fixes.row: "He saved others; He cannot save Himself": said to Jesus on the cross
fixes.why: These are the mocking form of 'Save yourself' ('You do not save?', 'Save Yourself and us') and are the Gospel counterpart of the row 'Not saved: no one to save ...'. The story's irony (He cannot save Himself, because He saves others) is a thing the teacher wants to see beside the OT 'does not save', not apart from it. Eight verses of one scene is a quotation, not a kind.
fixes.fix: Merge into 'Not saved: ...' keeping the cross quotation in its label: "... ; 'He saved others; He cannot save Himself', said to Jesus on the cross". Keep the note about whose words they are.

fixes.why: The participle 'the one who saves' is the same verb as 'The LORD saves the afflicted ... He saved me' and 10 verses are the 'I am your Savior' of the same Psalms and Isaiah passages. It is the Hebrew background of the NT noun and the arc 'there is no Savior but Me' -> 'God our Savior' needs both visible, but as a row of its own it floats apart from the rows it explains.
fixes.fix: Either merge into 'The LORD saves the afflicted, the needy ... ' (label adds '"my Savior", "there is no Savior but Me"') or keep as is if count is not binding; if merged, keep the note that the NT noun is a different word and is in the noun form.

fixes.row: God and salvation: "the salvation of the LORD" ... / Salvation is the LORD's: "belongs to the LORD" ...
fixes.why: Two rows, 34 and 17 verses, say the same thing: the salvation is God's (Rev 7:10, Ps 18:46, Ps 62:1 appear on both sides of the line). The text's own phrases ('the God of my salvation', 'belongs to the LORD') are two phrasings of one claim.
fixes.fix: Merge into one row 'Salvation is God's: "the salvation of the LORD", "the God of my salvation", "belongs to the LORD", "God our Savior"'. Keep the Rev 7:10 note.

fixes.row: Jesus called Savior; salvation in Christ / God and salvation
fixes.why: Titus 2:13 and 2 Pet 1:1 ('our great God and Savior Jesus Christ') sit in 'Jesus called Savior' and Titus 2:13 is also in the God row. Titus 1:3-4 and 3:4-6 pass the title 'Savior' between God and Jesus within a single letter. The reader is not told that these are the hub's hand-placed divine-person verses or that the hub does not decide whether the phrase names one person or two.
fixes.fix: Add a note on the Jesus row: "In Titus the title 'Savior' is given to God (1:3, 2:10, 3:4) and to Christ Jesus (1:4, 3:6); Titus 2:13 and 2 Pet 1:1 are in both rows because the phrase 'God and Savior' is read of one or of two. The page does not choose."

fixes.why: An unlabeled bucket of 18 verses holds three of the most-quoted verses on the theme. Acts 4:12 ('salvation is found in no one else') is the noun partner of the verb row for 'no other name' and belongs with 'Jesus called Savior; salvation in Christ'; John 4:22 ('salvation is from the Jews') is the hinge of the story's arc from Israel to the nations and fits 'Proclaimed, revealed, sent to the nations'; 1 Tim 4:10 is God as Savior of all and belongs in the God row. Leaving them in 'Every other use' hides the arc.
fixes.fix: Move Acts 4:12 to 'Jesus called Savior; salvation in Christ'; John 4:22 to 'Proclaimed, revealed, sent to the nations' (and widen the label 'from Israel to the nations'); 1 Tim 4:10 to the God row. Leave 2 Sam 10:11 / 1 Chr 19:12 (rescue in war), Job 5:4/5:11, Prov 11:14 in 'Every other use'.

fixes.why: 1 Thess 2:16 ('telling the Gentiles how they may be saved') is a plain case of 'Who is saved' and is stranded. Acts 27's ship is physical rescue, which is what 'Save a life' covers.
fixes.fix: Move 1 Thess 2:16 to 'Who is saved'. Acts 27:20, 27:31 to the merged life/soul row, which keeps the note that these are the ship in the storm.

fixes.row: Who is saved: "everyone", "the world", "all Israel"; "a few", "the remnant", "the chosen"
fixes.why: 'all Israel' is listed in the same breath as 'everyone' and 'the world' in the broad half of the label. Rom 11:26 is about a people and its relation to Rom 9:27's remnant. The label puts it in the wrong half and reads as a universal statement.
fixes.fix: Relabel as the text's phrases in two groups of the same weight: "'everyone', 'the world', 'all the ends of the earth'; 'all Israel', 'the remnant'; 'a few', 'the elect', 'the chosen'" or add to the note: "Rom 9:27 and 11:26 are Paul's two statements about Israel, one verse each."

fixes.row: Asked and answered: "Who then can be saved?" ... "Unless you are circumcised"
fixes.why: The label reads as a recipe: the questions and 'Believe' and 'Unless you are circumcised' sit on one line as if parallel answers. Acts 15:1 is a claim the same chapter answers at 15:11 and then 15:11 is in this hub's Jesus row. Also 'Who then can be saved?' (Matt 19:25) is a question the text itself answers one verse later without a word for 'saved'. Prov 20:22, 2 Thess 2:10 and Luke 8:12 are not questions or answers; they are about waiting, refusing and the devil.
fixes.fix: Relabel "Asked, and what is said in reply: ..." and drop "Unless you are circumcised" from the label, leaving Acts 15:1 in the row under the note that already names it as what certain men taught and Acts 15:11 as the reply. Move Prov 20:22, 2 Thess 2:10, Luke 8:12 to 'Said as still to come' or 'Who is saved' where they say what they say.

fixes.row: Saved, and works, deeds / Saved, and faith, believing, trust, refuge
fixes.why: Eighteen verses for faith against four for works, one of which (1 Cor 3:15) says 'work' only in the Greek. A reader counting rows will take the proportion as the text's. Three of the four are Titus 3:5, 2 Tim 1:9 and Jas 2:14, which pair works with faith or grace, not 'works' as an independent topic. The note covers Eph 2:9-10 but a reader scanning the rows sees an empty row.
fixes.fix: Keep both rows but put one sentence at the head of the works note: "Few verses with a word for 'saved' also name works; the verses on works that do not (Eph 2:9-10, Rom 3:28, Gal 2:16) are not here." Do not merge the pair (it would settle the order). The noun-form works row (14) already lists more.

fixes.why: A two-verse row where one verse is in the longer ending. Acts 2:38-41 and 16:30-33 are narrative the teacher expects to see as the story of how people are saved. They are named only in the note at best (Acts 2:40, 'be saved from this corrupt generation', is already in the hub in two other rows).
fixes.fix: Keep the row. In the note add Acts 2:40, which is in this hub, next to Acts 2:41 and name 2:38. Do not add the narratives as examples where the text has no word for 'saved'.

fixes.row: Where the Berean says "healed", "made well", "restore": the same Greek word
fixes.why: The label's 'same Greek word' is true and well done. It is incomplete in one place: Luke 7:50 ('Your faith has saved you', a forgiven woman) and Luke 17:19 ('your faith has made you well', a leper) are the same sentence in the same Gospel, one in the faith row and one here. The story shows that in Luke the one word carries both. Presenting them in two rows hides that from a reader who reads only one.
fixes.fix: Add to the note: "Luke 7:50 and Luke 17:19 are the same Greek words; the Berean prints 'saved' in one and 'made well' in the other."

fixes.row: Rock, light, strength, song, horn, shield, storehouse, helmet, garments, adorned, cup, walls, wells
fixes.why: Thirteen things in a label is a list to be scanned, not a kind. The Exod 15:2 -> Isa 12:2 echo ('my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation') is one of the Bible's clearest arcs and the label hides it.
fixes.fix: Relabel: "Images of salvation: 'my rock and my salvation', 'my light and my salvation', 'the horn of my salvation', 'the helmet of salvation', 'walls', 'wells'" and put Exod 15:2, Isa 12:2 first so the echo shows in the first four examples.

worker_points.point: 1. Whether salvation can be lost (tense split; 1 Cor 15:2 in both; John 10:28 and Heb 6:6 named in the note)
worker_points.why: The pair is an even hand as a layout, but the three Hebrew promises are read back into it (see fix) and the label mixes tense with condition. Naming one verse for each side in the note is balanced. Jude 5 stays in the Jesus row only; do not add it to row 18 (it is about the wilderness generation, and the textual variant 'Jesus'/'the Lord' is already in the note).

worker_points.point: 2. Election and choice in one list
worker_points.why: One list in the Bible's order is right. Do not split into two rows (that would be a row order that settles the question). Only the label needs fixing so 'all Israel' is not under 'everyone'.
Not a tilt in the text, but the proportion reads like one; add one sentence to the works note as above. Eph 2:9-10 in the note is enough.
Two verses is what the text gives for 'saved' and 'baptism' in one verse. Honest and adequately noted.
Do not give Acts 15:1 a row of its own. Keep the verse, change the label so it does not read as a recipe, and move the three verses that are not questions or answers.
Placement by hand is right. Acts 4:12 belongs with the Jesus-in-Christ noun row; 1 Tim 4:10 belongs in the God row. Titus 2:13 and 2 Pet 1:1 need a note since they appear under both persons.
The label is the Gospels' words, not a verdict on them. The fix is to merge it into 'Not saved', not to soften it.
A reader does not take it as 'healing is salvation'; the note says the page does not decide. This is an honest showing of one word with two renderings.

The verb form leads with Hebrew and the rows 'The LORD saves his people', 'A person saves' are presented as rescue, not type. Zech 9:9 left unmarked is right. Only the mixed-testament row ordering (Saved from ...) needs the Hebrew first.
Quoted in the note, so no reader has to guess.

worker_points.point: 11. God not saving (Judg 10:13, Hab 1:2, Jer 14:9, Ps 22:1, Ps 3:2, Isa 59:11)
worker_points.why: True to the text and the hardest part of its story. Keep.

missing.what: Romans 1:16-17: salvation and righteousness revealed in adjacent verses; the righteousness row has Rom 10:10 and Heb 11:7 but not Rom 1:16-17, the verse pair the Isaiah passages point to. The builder cannot join adjacent verses, so a note on the row naming Rom 1:17 would show the link.

Exodus-and-Red-Sea as the founding act: Exod 14:30 begins row 1 and Exod 15:2 is in the images row, but no note says that the later rows (Isa 12:2, Ps 106:8-10, Jude 5) go back to it. A note on row 1 naming Exod 14:30, 15:2 and Ps 106:8-10 would show the story's anchor.

Rom 8:24, 'in this hope we were saved', sits in the 'done' row only; the 'hope' and 'waiting' side of the story (Gen 49:18, Lam 3:26 in the noun row) has no verb counterpart, so the 'already and not yet' reads as a doctrine of tense rather than a text.

examples_checked: 32 of 33 rows' examples show their label in the Berean; 1 Cor 3:15 (the works row) shows it only through the row's note, which the row already carries; Jas 5:15 and Hos 14:3 were removed from rows they did not fit.
summary: The hub is true to the text, keeps the hard verses and takes no side on the divisive points; the fixes are the Hebrew promises read under the NT tense rows, the Hebrew-first order in mixed rows, a few labels that read as a recipe or a list (asked and answered, who is saved, images), and three verses in 'Every other use' that carry the arc (John 4:22, Acts 4:12, 1 Tim 4:10). On count, 33 rows can reach 28 by merging the cross into 'Not saved', life/soul into 'Saved from', 'God and salvation' with 'Salvation is the LORD's', and optionally the 'Savior' participle into the LORD row; going below 28 would mean merging the faith, works, grace, baptism and tense pairs, which are the contested ones and should stay apart.
